title: Repairing catastrophic repository damage
body:
Let's hypothetically I ran an errant `dd` command on the disk holding my repo, in such a way that after salvaging what was possible, a `borg check --repair` can't even complete:

```
Data integrity error: Invalid segment entry size 0 - too small [segment 56971, offset 110112635]
```

Deleting the index file and running `--repair --repository-only` gives the following:

```
Data integrity error: Invalid segment magic [segment 51735, offset 0]
```

What options do I have?

If the repo has to be written off, is it possible to repair it using a second repo that has largely been back up to with the same settings (I use `borgmatic` pointing to two repos). Is the most straightforward way just to copy the good repo over?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
dd is rather bad, because it could have damaged the filesystem.

What you can do is:
- transfer all repository files (`repo_dir/`) that are still readable somehow to a new disk (with a non-corrupt filesystem). `repo_dir/data/...` is the most important part (these are the segment files that have your data). this is also that the situation does not get worse than it already is. Only work on the copy, do not modify the original.
- also transfer the other files from `repo_dir/*` if that still works. if not, you maybe can also take them from a freshly initialized repository.
- if you used encryption, you will also need key and passphrase
- `borg check --repair` should rescue everything that is still valid. If a segment has an invalid magic, it should skip that segment and continue with the remaining ones. If it doesn't, look into the file with that number and check what's inside. If it does not start with "BORG...", it might be a completely different content from a damaged fs - in that case you can just delete that file.

There is no tooling to repair one borg 1.x repo using the data from another borg 1.x repo. Even if you used the same settings, the crypto key, the id key and the chunker secret will be different, so the chunks are not "compatible" (this has crypto security reasons). borg2 (and also borg 1.4.5+) offers "related repositories" that use the same id key and same chunker secret to enable that in future).

But if you have another backup repo, then you didn't lose data just because you lost the first one, right?

If you just want to have a working backup repo on the first disk:
- format the disk (erases all data, creates a valid filesystem)
- initialize a new borg repo on the first disk
- start from scratch on the first disk
- DO NOT "copy over" the disk2 repo to disk1 and update them both independently, you would break crypto security and confuse borg's caching if you do so.

A segment entry is just one part of the segment file (one file stores multiple objects inside it).

`borg check --repair` should try to recover such a segment, copying all valid entries to a new segment file, skipping the defect entry.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Unfortunately I've been "got" by borgmatic's `check --repair` behaviour differing from borg's. Running the borg command directly does indeed make (automatic) progress in the repair. This renders most of this issue invalid, although I'll confirm once the genuine repair has finished.

comments.author: reporter

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Can you tell what the problem was with borgmatic? Sounded a bit like unexpected behaviour?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Put simply: `borgmatic`'s `check` does not simply "passthrough" to `borg`. It can do other things, like trying to verify backups (eg using a sample of files) on a periodic basis. Some of this extra functionality requires `info`, even if the user (naively) just wants to run a straightforward `borg check`.

Ironically this isn't the first time this assumption has bit me: https://<redacted-host>/borgmatic-collective/borgmatic/issues/920#issuecomment-8712

The lesson of course is to always use `borg` directly when trying to diagnose a `borg` issue. I doubt `check` is the only command that does more than the `borg` equivalent.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: Requiring a successful `info` to run `check` doesn't seem like ideal design. Assuming borgmatic uses `info` only to obtain the repo ID, it could implement a fallback that still proceeds with `check` if `info` fails. Working with repos that might be damaged is the whole point of `check` after all. You might want to open an issue on their burg tracker about that.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: It's definitely worth a discussion, but without speaking for it too much `borgmatic` seems mainly designed to run a regular backup regime, so it may be out of scope to use it to diagnose and repair an exceptional case. In that sense I'd say the best improvement would be to rename its `check` command.
